blocks.clause: The Lord's supper is a sacrament of the New Testament,
blocks.note: letter printed as z; block starts at foot of left column and continues in right column

blocks.clause: feed upon his body and blood, to their spiritual nourishment and growth in grace;
have their union and communion with him confirmed;
testify and renew their thankfulness,
blocks.note: printed as [See above in a.]; references of a copied above (1 Cor. xi. 24 sits inside a)

blocks.clause: and engagement to God,
and their mutual love and fellowship each with other, as members of the same mystical body.
blocks.note: block begins at foot of p203 right column and continues on p204 (text read on p204: one bread, and one body)

blocks.clause: to take and eat the bread, and to drink the wine, in thankful remembrance that the body of Christ was broken and given, and his blood shed, for them.
blocks.note: first two references printed as [See before under a.] and [See before at a.]; the answer has only letter f (a-e belong to Q168)

blocks.clause: As the body and blood of Christ are not corporally or carnally present in, with, or under the bread and wine in the Lord's supper,
and yet are spiritually present to the faith of the receiver, no less truly and really than the elements themselves are to their outward senses;
do therein feed upon the body and blood of Christ, not after a corporal and carnal, but in a spiritual manner; yet truly and really,
printed: 1 Cor. xi. 24; Ver. 25; Ver. 26; Ver. 27; Ver. 28; Ver. 29
blocks.note: block runs from left column into right column

blocks.clause: while by faith they receive and apply unto themselves Christ crucified, and all the benefits of his death.
by examining themselves
of their being in Christ,
of their sins and wants;
blocks.note: Exod. xii. 15 is introduced by 'Compared with'

blocks.clause: of the truth and measure of their knowledge,
faith,
blocks.note: printed '1 Cor. xiii. 5. [See above in letter m.]' (m prints 2 Cor. xiii. 5: apparent misprint 1/2 in the source); Matt. xxvi. 28 follows

blocks.clause: repentance;
blocks.note: block continues on p205 (mourn for him ... 1 Cor. xi. 31)

blocks.clause: love to God and the brethren,
charity to all men,
forgiving those that have done them wrong;
of their desires after Christ,
and of their new obedience;
and by renewing the exercise of these graces,
blocks.note: block runs from foot of left column to top of right column

blocks.clause: by serious meditation,
and fervent prayer.
may have true interest in Christ, though he be not yet assured thereof;
printed: Ps. lxxvii. to verse 12; Ver. 1; Ver. 2; Ver. 3; Ver. 4; Ver. 7; Ver. 8; Ver. 9; Ver. 10
blocks.note: block starts on p205 right column and continues on p206 left column (Ps. lxxvii verses 9-10, Jonah)

blocks.clause: if he be duly affected with the apprehension of the want of it,
and unfeignedly desires to be found in Christ,
blocks.note: a printed asterisk precedes Ps. xlii. 1

blocks.clause: and to depart from iniquity:
for the relief even of weak and doubting Christians
he is to bewail his unbelief,
and labour to have his doubts resolved;
that he may be further strengthened.
may and ought to be kept from that sacrament, by the power which Christ hath left in his church,
printed: 1 Cor. chapter v. to the end
blocks.note: Matt. vii. 6, 1 Cor. v, Jude 23 and 1 Tim. v. 22 are introduced by 'Compared with' / 'And with'

blocks.clause: until they receive instruction, and manifest their reformation.
with all holy reverence and attention they wait upon God in that ordinance,
diligently observe the sacramental elements and actions,
blocks.note: Matt. xxvi. 28 introduced by 'Compared with', at top of right column

blocks.clause: heedfully discern the Lord's body,
and affectionately meditate on his death and sufferings,
and thereby stir up themselves to a vigorous exercise of their graces;
printed: 1 Cor. x. 3; Ver. 4; Ver. 5; Ver. 11; Ver. 14

blocks.clause: in judging themselves,
and sorrowing for sin;
in earnest hungering and thirsting after Christ,
feeding on him by faith,
receiving of his fulness,
trusting in his merits,
rejoicing in his love,
giving thanks for his grace;
in renewing of their covenant with God,
and love to all the saints.
is seriously to consider how they have behaved themselves therein, and with what success;
blocks.note: block begins at foot of p208 left column area (after the Q174 a block)

blocks.clause: if they find quickening and comfort, to bless God for it,
blocks.note: the quoted text prints 'Ver. 21' right after the reference list

blocks.clause: beg the continuance of it,
blocks.note: block begins at foot of left column and continues in right column

blocks.clause: watch against relapses,
fulfil their vows,
and encourage themselves to a frequent attendance on that ordinance:
but if they find no present benefit, more exactly to review their preparation to, and carriage at, the sacrament;
printed: Cant. v. 1; Ver. 2; Ver. 3; Ver. 4; Ver. 5; Ver. 6
Eccles. v. 1; Ver. 2; Ver. 3; Ver. 4; Ver. 5; Ver. 6
blocks.note: block continues on p209; a printed asterisk precedes Cant. v. 1

blocks.clause: in both which, if they can approve themselves to God and their own consciences, they are to wait for the fruit of it in due time:
blocks.note: clause text partly from p209 top; the clause words immediately before the superscript are 'they are to wait for the fruit of it in due time:'

blocks.clause: but, if they see they have failed in either, they are to be humbled,
blocks.note: block runs from left column into right column

blocks.clause: and to attend upon it afterwards with more care and diligence.
blocks.note: letter printed like numeral 1

blocks.clause: the author of both is God;
the spiritual part of both is Christ and his benefits;
both are seals of the same covenant,
blocks.note: block continues on p210 (Matt. xxvi. 28 ends there); Col. ii. 12 introduced by 'Compared with'

blocks.clause: are to be dispensed by ministers of the gospel, and by none other;
and to be continued in the church of Christ until his second coming.
baptism is to be administered but once, with water, to be a sign and seal of our regeneration and ingrafting into Christ,
and that even to infants;
blocks.note: block runs from left column into right column

blocks.clause: to represent and exhibit Christ as spiritual nourishment to the soul,
and to confirm our continuance and growth in him,
and that only to such as are of years and ability to examine themselves.
